verses.1: Unto the end. For the wine and oil presses. A Psalm of Asaph himself.
verses.2: Exult before God our helper. Sing joyfully to the God of Jacob.
verses.3: Take up a psalm, and bring forth the timbrel: a pleasing Psalter with stringed instruments.
verses.4: Sound the trumpet at the new moon, on the noteworthy day of your solemnity,
verses.5: for it is a precept in Israel and a judgment for the God of Jacob.
verses.6: He set it as a testimony with Joseph, when he went out of the land of Egypt. He heard a tongue that he did not know.
verses.7: He turned the burdens away from his back. His hands had been a slave to baskets.
verses.8: You called upon me in tribulation, and I freed you. I heard you within the hidden tempest. I tested you with waters of contradiction.
verses.9: My people, listen and I will call you to testify. If, O Israel, you will pay heed to me,
verses.10: then there will be no new god among you, nor will you adore a foreign god.
verses.11: For I am the Lord your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt. Widen your mouth, and I will fill it.
verses.12: But my people did not hear my voice, and Israel was not attentive to me.
verses.13: And so, I sent them away, according to the desires of their heart. They will go forth according to their own inventions.
verses.14: If my people had heard me, if Israel had walked in my ways,
verses.15: I would have humbled their enemies, as if it were nothing, and I would have sent my hand upon those who troubled them.
verses.16: The enemies of the Lord have lied to him, and their time will come, in every age.
verses.17: And he fed them from the fat of the grain, and he saturated them with honey from the rock. [ Psalm 81 ] (82)
